extends.description: Base ruleset to build on. Only 'default' is built in; anything else is read as a path.

allow.description: Vocabulary that never triggers a finding. A bare string is a regex that suppresses every rule on a matching line. A mapping narrows that to named rules, and can declare the same words to the semantic layer.

rules.description: Rule ids this entry silences. Omit for every rule. A rule id nothing answers to is a load error.

semantic.description: Also declare these words to the prompt-based layer, which reads no config of its own.

exclude.description: Glob patterns for files the linter skips entirely.

failOn.description: Severity threshold at which the exit code turns non-zero and the editor hook refuses a write. The default is advisory.

readability.description: Rules measured over sentence structure rather than matched at a point.

kind.description: Required on a new rule. Omit only when the entry overrides an inherited one.

maxWords.description: long-sentence and reply-length: the word count above which the rule fires.

known.description: unglossed-term only: names a reader already has. A project's entries add to the defaults rather than replacing them. Distinct from `allow`, which suppresses every rule on a matching line.

emphasis.description: unglossed-term only: ordinary words typed in capitals for emphasis, which are not acronyms. A project's entries add to the defaults rather than replacing them.

maxTerms.description: reader-load only: the count of distinct backticked names above which the rule fires.

maxMeanWords.description: reply-pace only: the average sentence length a whole reply may hold. Distinct from long-sentence, which judges one sentence: a reply where every sentence runs long breaks no single-sentence rule and still never lets up.

minWords.description: reply-pace only: the shortest reply worth measuring. A two-sentence answer has no pace.

maxClauses.description: unreadable-ask only: the count of subordinating clauses a closing question may carry before the reader has to unpack it.

chat.description: What the agent says in the chat window. Rendered into one output style per level, and checked by `lint --chat` and the chat hook. Distinct from every other section, which applies to text somebody reads later.

scope.description: The channel boundary, stated to the model. What chat covers, and what it does not.

level.description: Which level the AGENTS.md fragment carries and `init` selects. Must name an entry in `levels`.

levels.description: Renderings of one guidance list, ordered narrowest first. Each emits its own output style.

form.description: How this level renders. 'sections' gives every rule its own heading and paragraph. 'bullets' gives one checklist. Absent means 'sections'.

shape.description: The skeleton of a reply, rendered into the output style inside a fenced block. Every other entry in this section is a rule about a reply; this is the shape of one.

template.description: The skeleton itself. Rendered inside a fence, so placeholder text is never linted as prose.

guidance.description: Prose sections. A project overrides `levels` on an id to move a section between levels, or sets it empty to drop the section.

short.description: The rule in one imperative line. Used by the brief style, which renders a checklist instead of one heading per rule. Falls back to the first sentence of description.

examples.description: Worked replies, both halves. A `bad` half may contain a phrase `tells` bans, because an example of the reply nobody should write has to contain one. Rendered inside a blockquote, which the masking pass skips, so the style still lints clean under the rules it illustrates.

ask.description: What the reader asked, so the reply has something to be a reply to.

note.description: One line on what separates the two halves.

tells.description: Chat-only phrases, matched deterministically. The regex is generated from `phrases`, so the wording shown to a model and the wording matched by the linter cannot drift.

at.description: start anchors to the beginning of the reply, which is where an opener has to be. anywhere does not anchor.

avoid.description: Do-nots no pattern can reach, so they are stated rather than checked.

expand.description: When the shape gives way and the answer wins. Without these a shaping prompt clips answers that needed to be long.

judge.description: What the chat judge reads for beyond whether the length was earned. Each entry becomes a bullet in the generated prompt. Here rather than in the renderer because a prompt carrying wording no config governs is wording a project cannot change.

limits.description: Chat only: what one reply may ask the reader to carry. A document that runs long is doing its job, so these never apply outside a reply.

kind.description: Required on a new rule. Omit only when the entry overrides an inherited one.

maxWords.description: long-sentence and reply-length: the word count above which the rule fires.

known.description: unglossed-term only: names a reader already has. A project's entries add to the defaults rather than replacing them. Distinct from `allow`, which suppresses every rule on a matching line.

emphasis.description: unglossed-term only: ordinary words typed in capitals for emphasis, which are not acronyms. A project's entries add to the defaults rather than replacing them.

maxTerms.description: reader-load only: the count of distinct backticked names above which the rule fires.

maxMeanWords.description: reply-pace only: the average sentence length a whole reply may hold. Distinct from long-sentence, which judges one sentence: a reply where every sentence runs long breaks no single-sentence rule and still never lets up.

minWords.description: reply-pace only: the shortest reply worth measuring. A two-sentence answer has no pace.

maxClauses.description: unreadable-ask only: the count of subordinating clauses a closing question may carry before the reader has to unpack it.

failOn.description: Chat only: the tier at which a reply holds a turn. Separate from the top-level failOn, which decides whether a lint run fails a build. Unset falls back to it.

structures.description: Sentence shapes no regex can reach. Consumed by the semantic layer and the docs generator.

levelList.description: Which chat levels include this entry. An empty list drops it from every level, which is how a project turns one section off.

match.description: Regex applied case-insensitively to the masked text. Required unless the entry only overrides severity.

unless.description: Regexes that cancel a match. Checked against the surrounding line.

message.description: The rewrite hint shown with the finding.

perThousandWords.description: Makes this a rate rule: reported once per file, and only when the measured rate exceeds this threshold.

link.description: Where the finding sends the reader for the reasoning behind the rule.

reason.description: Why this project changed the rule. Set in a project config, never in the shipped ruleset. Printed next to the change in the generated policy document.
